notes: Dev RBox revision. Flips a property that holds by geometry (if A is diametrically opposite B, B is diametrically opposite A) to its opposite. antipode_of is also functional, but functionality gives no route back to symmetry, so the revision has no premise route back to the old property. The edit states the property only; the instance questions carry its meaning, with the instance fact in the prompt. The instances are real near-exact antipodal pairs that Wikipedia names (Tangier and Whangarei, Sanya and Arica) but text rarely does, so a model has no stored converse to answer from; the classic pairs (Spain and New Zealand, Christchurch and A Coruña) were avoided for that reason. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing, as in the RBox revision template: the direct question asks "asymmetric" (no, then yes), the first instance asks the converse (yes, then no), the second asks whether the fact rules out the converse (no, then yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Chinese 对跖点 has no direction built in, so the zh prompt keeps the English structure. Near unrelated asks the same property of another geography relation (a leak turns its "no" to "yes"); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. Spec note for the user: the edit makes the relation asymmetric, as the RBox revision template geography-replace-0904 does ("'Is twinned with' is asymmetric") and as README's RBox section allows for phrasing ("Is 'borders' asymmetric?"), but CRITERIA Rule 12 lists asymmetry as "not used anywhere" and README says asymmetry is not used. Here asymmetry is the edited property, not a derivation, and the instance answers do change (yes then no; no then yes), so the logic is sound. The alternative, "'Is the antipode of' is not symmetric", would leave the second instance ("Does that rule out ...?") at no before and after and every new answer at no. Kept as an exception for the user to decide.
